api-routing.test.mjs:
1. GET /api/rooms → 200, CT exact, body deepEqual {rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']}. Also with queries '/api/rooms?', '/api/rooms?x=1', '/api/rooms?/x' → same 200.

Verify after the POST variants that GET /api/bookings is still empty (nothing created).
3. 405 `method not allowed` (assertJsonError for non-HEAD; for HEAD check status 405 only): '/api/rooms' with POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS; '/api/bookings' with PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS; '/api/bookings/1' and '/api/bookings/abc' with GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS; '/' and '/app.js' with POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS. Explicitly a named test: GET /api/bookings/abc → 405. Also '/api/bookings/%31' GET → 405 (it is the DELETE route).
4. DELETE ids: create booking id 1 first (postBooking validBooking()). Then DELETE each of '/api/bookings/0', '01', '-1', '1.0', 'abc', '%31', '+1', '1e0', '0x1', '1%20', '99999999999999999999', '2' → 404 {error:'booking not found'}; after all of them GET /api/bookings still has booking 1 exactly. Then DELETE '/api/bookings/1?x=y' (query ignored) → 204 with empty body (body.length === 0); GET now empty; DELETE /api/bookings/1 again → 404 booking not found. Create booking (id 2) and delete '/api/bookings/2' → 204; a new booking then gets id 3.
5. Page: GET / → 200, CT exactly 'text/html; charset=utf-8', body bytes equal readFileSync of /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/public/index.html. GET /?x=1 → same. (Server is spawned with cwd = temp dir, proving files are found relative to server.mjs, not cwd — name the test that way.)
6. POST reply 201 has CT exact and exactly six keys: Object.keys sorted deepEqual ['date','end','id','room','start','title'] and typeof id 'number'.

api-bookings-list.test.mjs:
1. Empty: GET /api/bookings → 200, CT exact, {bookings: []}.
2. Sorting by date, then start, then room (Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos): POST in a scrambled order: Cosmos 2026-11-04 08:00-09:00; Aurora 2026-11-03 10:00-11:00; Borealis 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00; Cosmos 2026-11-03 09:00-09:30; Aurora 2026-11-03 09:00-09:30; Borealis 2026-11-10 07:00-08:00; Aurora 2026-11-09 23:00-23:59; Aurora 2025-12-31 12:00-13:00; Borealis 2026-11-03 09:00 ... (careful: no same-room overlap). Note: start sorts before room (Borealis 09:00 before Aurora 10:00). GET /api/bookings deepEqual the full expected array of complete booking objects (with ids) in the correct order.
3. ?date filter (same server data): '?date=2026-11-03' → only those, sorted; '?date=2026-11-03&date=2026-11-04' → the 2026-11-03 ones (first value wins); '?x=1&date=2026-11-04' → only 11-04; '?Date=2026-11-03' → all bookings (param name is case sensitive, ignored); '?date=2026%2D11%2D03' → same as 2026-11-03 (decoded); '?date=2030-01-01' → {bookings: []}; '?' → all; '?dates=2026-11-03' → all.

5. Valid ?date values accepted (200): '?date=2000-02-29', '?date=2096-02-29', '?date=2000-01-01', '?date=2099-12-31'.

content.content: 19:API 20-- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21-- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22-- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23-- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24-- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25-- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26-- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27-- `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28-- `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29-- Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30-- A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31-- Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32- 33-Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34-1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35-2.
